newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil financial buyouts show confidence-cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil financial buyouts show confidence-cenbank.

text.p: The purchases of a Brazilian bank and a brokerage by two major international banks is a sign of international confidence in the Brazilian economy and in the banking sector, a Central Bank director said.

Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) approved Thursday a proposed purchase by Deutsche Bank AG of a brokerage belonging to bank Banco Irmaos Guimaraes, which has been operating under Central Bank administration.
Deutsche would pay 5.1 million reais for the brokerage which, unlike its parent bank, is in good financial shape, Central Bank Norms Director Alkimar Moura said.

The CMN also approved a proposed 13.8 million-reais buyout by CS Holding affiliate CS First Boston of Banco Investcorp which is in the process of being liquidated but would operate as a commercial and investment bank under its new owners.
The deal included a Central Bank loan of 7.6 million reais to CS First Boston repayable over five years with interest set at 6.0 percent over Brazil's Treasury Rate, Moura said.
Both purchases must now be approved by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
"The entry of these foreign banks shows there is confidence in the Brazilian economy and in the financial system," Moura said.
